## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Collections
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Collections containers
//  - Collections grids
//  - Collections indexable
//  - Derived row access over the IJagged interface
//  - Collections sampling

library Collections
{
    //==
    // # Collections containers
    //
    // Derived functionality for the container-shape interfaces
    // (`collections.concepts.plato`): sub-range helpers built on Slice,
    // self-concatenation, negated membership and key tests, and the LIFO/FIFO
    // conveniences (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abstract_data_type).

    //==
    // # ISliceable
    //
    // Contiguous sub-range helpers built on the half-open Slice(from, exclusiveTo).
    // The end-relative helpers (Skip, TakeLast, DropLast) read Count, which
    // ISliceable now inherits from ICountable.
    // Note: these return the bare interface type ISliceable rather than the concrete
    // implementing type, so chained calls (self.Take(n).Take(m)) resolve against
    // the interface surface and type-check; the concrete type is simply not recovered.
    //
    // `SubRange(start, end)` used to sit here as the endpoint form over a
    // count-based Slice. plato-378 made Slice itself the endpoint form, which
    // made the two identical, so SubRange is gone.

    // The first `count` elements. Precondition: 0 <= count <= Count.
    Take(self: ISliceable, count: Integer): ISliceable
        => self.Slice(0, count);

    // Everything after the first `count` elements.
    // Precondition: 0 <= count <= Count.
    //
    // Spelled `Drop` until plato-378. One tree should not spell one operation
    // two ways, and `Skip` is the spelling `Array` already uses for exactly this
    // (`primitives.library.plato`) — so `Skip` removes from the front and
    // `DropLast` from the back, in both vocabularies.
    Skip(self: ISliceable, count: Integer): ISliceable
        => self.Slice(count, self.Count);

    // The last `count` elements. Precondition: 0 <= count <= Count.
    TakeLast(self: ISliceable, count: Integer): ISliceable
        => self.Slice(self.Count - count, self.Count);

    // Everything except the last `count` elements.
    // Precondition: 0 <= count <= Count.
    DropLast(self: ISliceable, count: Integer): ISliceable
        => self.Slice(0, self.Count - count);

    //==
    // # IConcatenable
    //
    // Joining helpers built on Concat(a, b).

    // The collection joined to itself end to end.
    Doubled(self: IConcatenable): IConcatenable
        => self.Concat(self);

    //==
    // # ISet
    //
    // Membership helpers built on Contains(item).

    // True when the item is not a member.
    DoesNotContain(self: ISet<$T>, item: $T): Boolean
        => self.Contains(item).Not;

    //==
    // # IMap
    //
    // Key-lookup helpers. IMap inherits ICountable, so IsEmpty / IsNotEmpty
    // apply directly.

    // True when the map has no entry for the given key.
    DoesNotContainKey(self: IMap<$TKey, $TValue>, key: $TKey): Boolean
        => self.ContainsKey(key).Not;

    //==
    // # IStack
    //
    // LIFO helpers. Push / Pop return new stacks.

    // Replace the top element: pop the current top, then push the new item.
    // Precondition: the stack is not empty.
    ReplaceTop(self: IStack<$T>, item: $T): IStack<$T>
        => self.Pop.Push(item);

    //==
    // # IQueue
    //
    // FIFO helpers. Enqueue / Dequeue return new queues.

    // Move the front element to the back, preserving the order of the rest.
    // Precondition: the queue is not empty.
    Rotate(self: IQueue<$T>): IQueue<$T>
        => self.Enqueue(self.Front).Dequeue;

    //==
    // # Collections grids
    //
    // Derived functionality for the multi-dimensional IIndexable interfaces
    // (`collections.concepts.plato`): bounds checks, corner-cell access,
    // and the row-major flat-index conversions
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Row-_and_column-major_order) for 2D grids, 3D
    // volumes and 4D hypervolumes.

    //==
    // # IIndexable2D
    //
    // Cell access, bounds checks, and row-major flat-index conversions for a
    // column x row grid.

    // True when (column, row) lies within the grid.
    IsValidCell(self: IIndexable2D<$T>, column: Integer, row: Integer): Boolean
        => column >= 0 && column < self.ColumnCount
        && row >= 0 && row < self.RowCount;

    // The row-major flat index of cell (column, row): row * ColumnCount + column.
    FlattenIndex(self: IIndexable2D<$T>, column: Integer, row: Integer): Integer
        => row * self.ColumnCount + column;

    // The (column, row) pair for a row-major flat index. Inverse of FlattenIndex.
    UnflattenIndex(self: IIndexable2D<$T>, index: Integer): Tuple2<Integer, Integer>
        => (index % self.ColumnCount, index / self.ColumnCount);

    // The top-left cell (0, 0). Precondition: the grid is not empty.
    FirstCell(self: IIndexable2D<$T>): $T
        => self.At(0, 0);

    // The bottom-right cell. Precondition: the grid is not empty.
    LastCell(self: IIndexable2D<$T>): $T
        => self.At(self.ColumnCount - 1, self.RowCount - 1);

    //==
    // # IIndexable3D
    //
    // Cell access and bounds checks for a column x row x layer volume.

    // True when (column, row, layer) lies within the volume.
    IsValidCell(self: IIndexable3D<$T>, column: Integer, row: Integer, layer: Integer): Boolean
        => column >= 0 && column < self.ColumnCount
        && row >= 0 && row < self.RowCount
        && layer >= 0 && layer < self.LayerCount;

    // The row-major flat index of cell (column, row, layer):
    // (layer * RowCount + row) * ColumnCount + column.
    FlattenIndex(self: IIndexable3D<$T>, column: Integer, row: Integer, layer: Integer): Integer
        => (layer * self.RowCount + row) * self.ColumnCount + column;
```
